example.name: extract_method_from_long_function
example.description: Refactoring a long method by extracting smaller, focused methods
example.context: When a single method is doing multiple things and has high complexity
example.scenario: User has a long order processing function with validation, calculation, and discount logic all mixed together
example.explanation: This refactoring extracts three focused methods (calculateOrderTotals, calculateDiscount, calculateTax, calculateShipping) from a single large method. Each extracted method has a single responsibility, making the code more testable and maintainable. The original processOrder method now orchestrates these operations clearly.

example.name: replace_conditional_with_polymorphism
example.description: Replacing complex conditional logic with polymorphic objects
example.context: When you have type-specific behavior scattered throughout conditional statements
example.scenario: Payment processing with different calculation methods for different customer types
example.explanation: This refactoring replaces complex conditional logic with the Strategy pattern. Each shipping calculation method is encapsulated in its own class, making the code more extensible and easier to test. The calculateShipping function now delegates to the appropriate strategy based on customer type.

example.name: break_down_large_class
example.description: Systematically breaking down a large class into smaller, focused classes
example.context: When you have a monolithic class that handles multiple concerns and has grown too large
example.scenario: A UserService class that handles user management, validation, and database operations all in one place
example.explanation: This example shows systematic refactoring of a large class. First, characterization tests are written to ensure behavior is preserved. Then the class is broken down step by step: validation logic is extracted, database operations are extracted, and finally the main class is refactored to use these components. Each step maintains test coverage and functionality.

example.name: legacy_code_modernization
example.description: Modernizing old code patterns while preserving functionality
example.context: When working with legacy code that uses outdated patterns
example.scenario: Modernizing callback-based code to use Promises and async/await
example.explanation: This refactoring modernizes callback-based code to use modern Promises and async/await patterns. The behavior is preserved, but the implementation is cleaner and more maintainable. The refactoring maintains the same external interface while improving internal structure.
